scope: iOS networking, retained data, native uploads, chat viewport/read state, auth-origin isolation, drafts, and server/worker push authorization

method.kind: deterministic unit/contract A/B plus source-backed bounds
notes: Request-count comparisons use the previous 2,000 ms foreground poll and the implemented 60,000 ms healthy-stream safety reconciliation.
Native upload memory is a transport contract result, not an Instruments RSS sample: picker base64 is disabled and expo-file-system File.upload owns the file-backed request outside JavaScript.
Visual parity for this slice is guarded by retaining the existing screen/composer surfaces and focused source tests; final device CUA remains a release gate.

originIsolation.snapshotCache: server URL filtered with epoch guards and two-slot journal
originIsolation.drafts: v2 normalized origin plus channel ID
originIsolation.authWrites: serialized and generation guarded; latest operation wins, tokens are persisted with their normalized server, and unbound legacy bearers are discarded
originIsolation.authModeDiscovery: same-origin checks and SecureStore writes are monotonic; required-mode revocation deletes a stale disabled grant before writing its tombstone, only a transport exception may reuse disabled mode, and every malformed or live non-disabled response fails closed
originIsolation.requestCredentials: each request reports the bearer it actually used; a 401 clears authentication only if that exact server and bearer are still current
originIsolation.providerMutations: every post-await provider state commit requires the captured client identity and connection epoch
originIsolation.pushOperations: native preflight rechecks a retiring-client guard; issued requests are tracked per client and use a cleanup client with the captured origin credential
originIsolation.oldPushInstallation: registration identity creation is single-flight; client retirement remains ordered, while durable privacy is enforced by binding required-mode devices to a Better Auth session
originIsolation.pushDeliveryAuthorization: eligibility derives from the server's current OPENBOT_AUTH_MODE: required mode accepts only required registrations with a present, unexpired session, while disabled mode accepts only explicit disabled-mode registrations; undefined or invalid worker configuration fails closed to required
originIsolation.pushSignOutOrdering: worker dispatch and server session retirement share one bounded PostgreSQL advisory lock; the worker row-locks and revalidates devices immediately before Expo delivery and holds the transaction through the 15-second-capped request, while sign-out disables every bound device under the same 20-second-capped lock before invalidating the session
originIsolation.pushMigration: legacy rows migrate authRequired=true with no session, so they are fail-closed until the next foreground registration; disabled-mode registration explicitly restores delivery without a session

recoveryCases.observedEventBootstrapFailure: reconnect cursor remains last committed and bounded retry is scheduled
recoveryCases.bootstrapProjectionRace: the server captures its replay cursor before starting projection reads, so a concurrent commit is replayed rather than skipped
recoveryCases.bootstrapBelowObservedEvent: normal commits below the highest observed event are rejected and retried
recoveryCases.cachedCursorAheadOfRestoredServer: snapshot.required resets the ledger and accepts the authoritative lower cursor
recoveryCases.initialBootstrapFailureWithoutCache: bounded exponential retry starts before live-stream readiness
recoveryCases.earlySseConsumerFailure: response reader is cancelled and lock released
recoveryCases.serverSwitchDuringNewSignIn: old SecureStore delete completes or is superseded before the new token write; delayed old-origin login and validation results are rejected
recoveryCases.sameOriginReauthentication: a delayed 401 carrying the retired bearer cannot clear a newer session on the same server
recoveryCases.authModeResponseReordering: a delayed disabled response/write cannot overwrite a newer required observation, and a required persistence failure first removes the stale disabled grant
recoveryCases.serverSwitchDuringMutation: delayed create, send, update, history, read, reaction, widget, upload, approval, routine, and computer results cannot enter or drive the new origin's state
recoveryCases.disabledAuthOfflineColdStart: a previously observed disabled origin passes AuthGate during discovery network failure and can hydrate its offline snapshot; a different origin or live unknown response cannot bypass login
recoveryCases.delayedPushAfterSwitchOrSignOut: the stale client never receives the new origin's bearer; a late required-mode registration cannot remain deliverable after its bound session is deleted, even if client cleanup times out
recoveryCases.automatic401OrSessionExpiry: server-side session filtering prevents an expired, revoked, or automatically logged-out session's device from being enqueued or sent without relying on client cleanup
recoveryCases.concurrentFirstPushRegistration: overlapping startup, foreground, and token-change registration calls share one persisted installation ID, so retirement cannot orphan a second identity
recoveryCases.disabledToRequiredAuthTransition: delivery uses the current server mode rather than the mode persisted at registration, so a pre-transition disabled registration stops being eligible immediately
recoveryCases.signOutDuringPushDispatch: the shared advisory lock orders sign-out completion after any already-authorized bounded Expo request; otherwise the worker observes the disabled row during its final in-transaction revalidation and skips delivery

boundedResiduals: A notification already handed to Expo cannot be recalled. The shared advisory lock ensures that such an authorized send finishes before sign-out reports completion; queued or not-yet-authorized notifications are revalidated and skipped after retirement.
Existing auth-disabled installations are intentionally fail-closed by the migration until that app next opens and re-registers with the server's explicit disabled mode.
